questions.q: An advantage of the burn-up chart is that: *

o.t: It can show the remaining work to be done.
It can show changes in project cost.
It can show changes in scope.
It can show the individual team members' performance.

questions.e: A burn-up chart tracks completed work and the total scope of the project. Unlike a burn-down chart, which only shows remaining work, a burn-up chart displays changes in scope over time, helping teams manage scope creep effectively.

questions.q: During a meeting with the sponsor, the project manager gets feedback on the latest prototype and commits to creating a revised version accordingly within three weeks. Which of the following development approaches is the project manager using? *
questions.e: An iterative approach allows for incremental refinements based on feedback. The project manager commits to a revised prototype, meaning continuous improvements are made rather than delivering everything at once.

questions.q: No matter what type of project they are managing or what type of challenges they might face, an agile project manager should make sure that the cross-functional team is always focused on: *
questions.e: Agile emphasizes delivering customer value early and often. Frequent delivery (A) and quality (C) are important, but value delivery is the ultimate goal.

questions.q: A project manager is leading an Agile project where the team works in a continuous flow rather than using iterations. This approach proved to be less prescriptive and disruptive to the team. Which Agile framework is the project manager using? *
questions.e: Kanban follows a continuous flow model where work is pulled as capacity allows, rather than following time-boxed iterations like Scrum.ation boundaries.

questions.q: For their new outdoor fitness park project, the project manager uses an approach that yields frequent smaller deliverables throughout the span of the project. What type of project development approach are they using? *
questions.e: Incremental development delivers working parts of the product at regular intervals. This differs from iterative (C), which allows modifications to past work.

questions.q: The following chart was presented during a retrospective meeting. Which of the following statements is true regarding this chart? *

o.t: This burnup chart shows that there is work left at the end of the sprint
This burnup chart shows that the planned work is completed before the end of the sprint
This burndown chart shows that there is work left at the end of the sprint
This burndown chart shows that the planned work is completed before the end of the sprint

questions.e: A burndown chart tracks the amount of work remaining in a sprint. The chart shows that not all story points were completed by the end of the sprint, indicating that there is still work left.

questions.q: This is the first time the project manager adopts the scrum framework for the project execution. One of the team members asks the project manager when a Sprint is considered completed. What should be the project manager’s response? *

o.t: When all product backlog items are completed
When all the tasks in the sprint are completed
When the sprint’s defined timebox ends
When all product backlog items meet the Definition of Done (DoD)

questions.e: A Sprint is time-boxed, meaning it always ends after the set duration (typically 2-4 weeks) regardless of task completion.

questions.q: A team, with no defined roles, uses a board and cards to categorize tasks into “To do”, “Doing”, and “Done”. Without too many restrictions, team members grab a card from the “To do” list and begin to work. What agile framework is being described? *
questions.e: Kanban uses a visual board where team members pull tasks from "To Do" to "Doing" and "Done" without strict role definitions.

questions.q: Using an Agile approach, where should product requirements be documented? *
questions.e: In Agile, requirements evolve and are stored in the product backlog, managed by the Product Owner.

questions.q: An experienced scrum master is often asked “How long should a sprint be?” to which they always respond by saying “It depends, you should initially find a balance that works for the team, but typically an agile scrum sprint is ____________ long.” *
questions.e: Scrum sprints are generally 2-4 weeks long to allow quick iterations while maintaining predictability.

questions.q: Since switching to the agile approach, a project manager has been encouraging their team to be self-organizing by allowing them to decide on how to execute their assigned work. What is the main aspect of a self-organizing team? *

o.t: It gives more responsibility to the project manager
It gives more responsibility to the Agile team
It allows the team to deliver a working product without external dependencies
It gives team members higher visibility of the product

questions.e: Agile teams self-organize, meaning they determine how to execute their work rather than being micromanaged.

questions.q: In order to handle high levels of change and ensure the active participation of all interested parties, a project manager adopts a change-driven project development approach, which is also known as: *
questions.e: An adaptive approach is used in Agile to handle high uncertainty and frequent changes.

questions.q: In projects following the Scrum framework, which of the following questions won’t be asked to team members during daily stand-ups? *

o.t: What have you completed since the last stand-up?
What will you complete until the next stand-up?
What do we need to finish as a team?

questions.e: Scrum stand-ups focus on individual contributions, identifying progress and obstacles.

questions.q: During a Sprint, the development team realizes that completing all committed backlog items within the Sprint is not feasible due to unforeseen complexities. The Product Owner insists that all items must be completed within the Sprint. What is the best course of action for the Scrum Team? *

o.t: The Scrum Master should intervene and extend the Sprint duration to accommodate the work.
The Development Team should work overtime to ensure all backlog items are completed as per the commitment.
The Scrum Team should inspect and adapt by negotiating with the Product Owner to reprioritize and focus on completing the highest-value work.
The Development Team should drop lower-priority items without informing the Product Owner and focus on the most crucial backlog items.

questions.e: In Scrum, transparency, inspection, and adaptation are key principles. If the team cannot complete all backlog items due to unforeseen complexities, the right approach is to inspect the situation and adapt accordingly. The Product Owner and Development Team should collaborate to reprioritize work, ensuring the highest-value backlog items are delivered within the Sprint.

questions.q: During the project planning phase, the scrum master, product owner, and cross-functional team members select the backlog items to be executed in the next sprint. In such a team, who commits to delivering business value by the end of the sprint? *
questions.e: The team commits to delivering value, while the Product Owner prioritizes backlog items.

questions.q: The role of the product owner in an Agile project is: *

o.t: Coordinating the work of the sprint and running the team
Having a vested interest in the project and its outcomes and interfacing with stakeholders
Representing the business unit, customer, or end-user
Completing the backlog items and signing up tasks based on established priorities

questions.e: The Product Owner ensures that the team builds the right product by working closely with stakeholders.

questions.q: An associate project manager is working for a digital design agency specializing in branding and packaging. In their current project, the project manager uses an approach that implies sharing partially completed work with the client in order to obtain early feedback and modify the product accordingly. The project manager is using a(n)____________ approach. *
questions.e: An iterative approach refines the product by sharing early versions for feedback before finalizing.

questions.q: For their new project, a project manager decided to create a Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), define and sequence all activities, and then execute tasks in month-long cycles. The sponsor can change 30% of the subsequent cycle’s scope of work with no need for a change request. Which of the following approaches is being adopted? *
questions.e: A hybrid approach combines predictive planning (WBS, sequencing) with adaptive flexibility (30% scope change).

questions.q: In an adaptive project, the business analyst has written use cases before the sprint starts. This is known as: *
questions.e: ehavior-Driven Development (BDD) is an Agile software development process that encourages collaboration between developers, QA, and non-technical or business participants in a software project. Use cases written before the sprint starts to describe the expected behavior of the system align with BDD practices.

questions.q: Which of the following is the top priority for an agile project? *

o.t: Working collaboratively with customer and having a lightweight contract.
Satisfying the customer through delivery of valuable product.
Providing working software and accurate documentation.
Responding to change and following an adaptive plan.

questions.e: According to the Agile Manifesto, the highest priority is to satisfy the customer through early and continuous delivery of valuable software. This focus ensures that the project consistently delivers value and meets customer needs.

questions.q: Who should know the most about the progress toward a business objective or a release in a scrum team? *
questions.e: The Product Owner is responsible for maximizing the value of the product and ensuring that the team is delivering on the business objectives. They have the most insight into the progress toward a business objective or a release, as they are closely involved in managing the product backlog and prioritizing work based on business goals.

questions.q: The project sponsor wants to know what will the project deliver in each release and when these releases will be completed. Which agile artifact would address his needs? *
questions.e: The Product Roadmap is an agile artifact that provides a high-level overview of the product's development plan. It outlines what will be delivered in each release and the timeline for these releases, addressing the sponsor's need to understand the project's deliverables and schedule.

questions.q: ABC Organization has decided to initiate a new project to develop an infrastructure solution which includes power systems that are energy efficient, high availability , and scalable. The solution involves high degree of innovation. Which of the following development approaches will most fit this project? *

o.t: There is not enough information to decide.

questions.e: For highly innovative projects, an adaptive (Agile) approach is best due to the high degree of uncertainty.

questions.q: The daily standup usually takes more than 15 minutes because the product owner takes some time distributing tasks to the team member. Which of the following is the best course of action? *

o.t: The scrum master should distribute tasks to team member after the daily standup.
Extend the daily standup to 30 minutes.
The scrum master should distribute tasks to team member before the daily standup.
The scrum master should ask the product owner not attend the daily standup and not to distribute tasks to team members.

questions.e: In Scrum, the daily standup (or Daily Scrum) is a time-boxed event of 15 minutes where the Development Team synchronizes their work and plans for the next 24 hours. The Product Owner should not distribute tasks during this meeting. Instead, the team members should be self-organizing and take responsibility for selecting their own tasks. The Scrum Master should guide the Product Owner to respect this aspect of the Scrum framework.

questions.q: What is the purpose of the questions asked during the daily standup? *

o.t: Define impediments and discuss planned work.

questions.e: Daily stand-ups focus on what was done, what will be done, and any blockers preventing progress.
